//: The canonical auth email configuration, as one source of truth for the CI shape test (config/auth-templates.test.mjs) and the live check (scripts/check-auth-config.mjs). Keys are Supabase Management API auth-config keys, verbatim, so the check can PATCH exactly these and nothing else -- see ./README.md on why a partial PATCH matters.

settings.//: Six digits because app/(auth)/verify.tsx enables its button on /^\d{6}$/ and nothing else. The project was issuing eight at one point, which would have produced a code that arrives and cannot be typed. Ten minutes because both bodies say 'expires in 10 minutes', and copy that disagrees with configuration is a support ticket.

limits.//: VERIFIED, NEVER APPLIED. Abuse and capacity controls the client depends on, recorded as production had them when read on 2026-09-21 (`supabase config diff`: auth.email.max_frequency 1m0s, auth.rate_limit.email_sent 30). check-auth-config.mjs fails on a difference and --apply refuses to write these: they are founder decisions made in the dashboard, and a repair script that quietly put one back would undo a deliberate raise. To change one, change it in the dashboard AND here (and anything under clientDependsOn) in one reviewed change. The 2026-09-21 signup incident was a client built for a 30-second cooldown against a server enforcing 60, with nothing written down for either to be checked against.

smtp_max_frequency.unit: seconds between two emails to one address
smtp_max_frequency.onDrift: The Resend code countdown no longer matches the server. Shorter than the server: the button goes live and every tap before the server's time is refused with over_email_send_rate_limit (the verify screen now re-arms from GoTrue's remaining seconds, so it recovers, but the button still promises a send it cannot make). Longer: people wait for nothing.

rate_limit_email_sent.unit: auth emails per hour, whole project
rate_limit_email_sent.clientDependsOn: src/features/auth/methods.ts: an over_email_send_rate_limit with no seconds in it is read as this ceiling and answered with 'try again in a few minutes, or continue with Apple or Google'
rate_limit_email_sent.onDrift: Capacity changed without a record. Raising it needs the email provider's own quota to carry the new number (Resend's free plan stops at 100 a day); lowering it blocks more first sign-ins. Either way, update this value in the same change.

//flow: ONE client call reaches BOTH of these. sendEmailCode calls signInWithOtp with shouldCreateUser: true, and GoTrue picks the template by the address: no account yet -> Confirm signup, account already -> Magic Link. Both are exercised in ordinary use, both must be right, and both codes are verified with the same EmailOtpType ('email') -- which is why verifiedAs is identical below and is not a per-template choice any more.

templates.name: Confirm signup
templates.reaches: an address with no account yet -- everybody signing in to Bingd for the first time
templates.subject: Your bingd. sign-in code

templates.name: Magic Link
templates.reaches: an address that already has an account -- everybody coming back
templates.subject: Your bingd. sign-in code
